teams.heading: Fiji fall to Japan in Pacific Nations Cup final in Tokyo
teams.body: Fiji fell 20-15 to Japan in a tense Pacific Nations Cup final on Saturday in Tokyo, failing to defend their crown. Despite a yellow card for Mesake Doge, the Flying Fijians led 12-10 at half-time following tries from Virimi Vakatawa and Tevita Ikanivere. After Ben Gunter put the hosts ahead, Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula levelled the score with a penalty. However, Samisoni Tua crossed the line with 10 minutes remaining to secure the title for Japan, ending Fiji's run of consecutive titles.

lead.why: Japan's dramatic victory over Fiji in the Pacific Nations Cup final is the day's primary men's international rugby story.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards joins England Women as defence consultant for WXV campaign
teams.body: The England women's team has pulled off a major coup by appointing Shaun Edwards as a defence consultant for the WXV campaign. The 59-year-old, who left France in June, will assist head coach John Mitchell, who described his credentials as "exceptional". Edwards is already in situ as the Red Roses prepare to face New Zealand this Saturday at Allianz Stadium, ahead of next month's fixtures in Canada and the United States.

teams.heading: Pauline Bourdon Sansus leads France Women to comeback win against Australia
teams.body: France Women staged a miraculous comeback to beat Australia 29-26 on Saturday despite a burning bus delaying the second half. Trailing 19-0 and temporarily reduced to just 11 players following a red card and three yellows, the hosts rallied through Pauline Bourdon Sansus to stun the Wallaroos. France conceded six cards in total but finished the match with 17 unanswered points in the final quarter. The victory maintains their momentum ahead of upcoming tests against the Black Ferns.

lead.why: It is the most significant recent result, featuring a dramatic 19-point comeback and unusual off-field disruptions.

teams.heading: Sean Jansen commits to Connacht with new long-term deal until 2029
teams.body: Ireland number eight Sean Jansen has handed Connacht a significant boost by signing a two-year contract extension, securing his future at the club until 2029. The back-rower, who made his international debut against Japan earlier this year, was voted Connacht’s Player of the Year last season after scoring 12 tries. Head coach Stuart Lancaster hailed the agreement as a “statement of intent,” noting that Jansen’s best years remain ahead of him following his impressive breakthrough into the national squad.

teams.heading: Italy women dominate Japan with comprehensive 55-21 opening tournament victory
teams.body: The Italy women's side opened their WXV Global Series campaign in style with a convincing 55-21 win over Japan at Stadio Omero Tognon. After conceding early, the Azzurre responded with a clinical display, including a first-half try fest that saw them pull away to a commanding lead. Captain Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi celebrated her 50th cap by crossing the whitewash in the second half, helping Italy register their highest-ever points tally against the Sakura XV in a dominant performance.

teams.heading: Sisilia Tuipulotu eyes Lions selection after dominant Wales women's performance
teams.body: Wales women's prop Sisilia Tuipulotu has identified a spot on next year's inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour as her top priority. The Harlequins tight-head produced a world-class, two-try display in Friday's 50-19 WXV Global Series win over South Africa, catching the eye of Lions head coach Jo Yapp. Having credited a rigorous six-week pre-season for her return to form, the 23-year-old is now focused on maintaining that momentum when Wales women face the USA this Saturday.

teams.heading: Jordan Petaia returns to Wallabies squad following injury-plagued NFL stint
teams.body: Utility back Jordan Petaia has been recalled to the 34-man Wallabies squad after his transition to the NFL was curtailed by a misdiagnosed hamstring injury. Petaia, who last represented Australia at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, spent four months with the Los Angeles Chargers before a tendon issue necessitated a return to rugby. Now with Japan Rugby League One side Urayasu D-Rocks, Petaia is fully focused on securing his place under head coach Les Kiss ahead of next year's home World Cup.

teams.heading: Japan defeat Fiji to claim Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup
teams.body: Japan secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019, edging Fiji 20-15 in a physical encounter at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. After trailing by two at the break, the Brave Blossoms regained the lead through a Ben Gunter try before Samisoni Tua crossed in the final 10 minutes to seal victory. Captain Naoto Saito hailed the win as a potential turning point for his young squad, stating, “It’s a great breakthrough to create history for Japan. It gives this young team great confidence.”

lead.why: Japan's first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 represents the most significant recent development for the men's side.

teams.heading: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea sidelined indefinitely after shoulder surgery confirmed
teams.body: New Zealand Rugby has confirmed that All Blacks skipper Ardie Savea faces a lengthy recovery following surgery on a dislocated shoulder. Sustained during the third Test against the Springboks, the injury ruled the 32-year-old out of the final tour match and will keep him out of next month's Bledisloe Cup fixtures. With rehabilitation for such procedures typically spanning six months, his availability for the upcoming Nations Championship remains in significant doubt, leaving a notable void in the team’s loose forward rotation.

lead.why: The injury to captain Ardie Savea is the most significant news affecting the squad's immediate future.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus releases Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende early
teams.body: Coach Rassie Erasmus has sent two first-choice stalwarts home ahead of this Sunday’s Test against the Wallabies in Perth. Flank Pieter-Steph du Toit and centre Damian de Allende will return to South Africa to spend time with their families following their demanding workload during the recent series against the All Blacks. Erasmus confirmed that he has sufficient cover within his travelling squad to manage the rotation for the upcoming fixture as the team looks to maintain its momentum.
